en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa: Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 16.40. The Triplet on Having the Path as Object, and the Couplets on Root-Condition The Triplet on Having the Path as Object, and the Couplets on Root-Condition: [Textual Excerpts] 1. *Maggārammaṇattika* (Triplet on Having the Path as Object): 1.1. Which states have the Path as their object? 1.2. Which states do not have the Path as their object? 1.3. Which states both have and do not have the Path as their object? 2. *Hetuduka* (Couplets on Root-Condition): 2.1. Which states are roots? 2.2. Which states are not roots? ... 2.17. Which states are root-conditions? 2.18. Which states are not root-conditions? [End of Section] Note: This excerpt represents the structural headings and initial entries for the specified sections of the *Paṭṭhāna-pakaraṇa*. The full text would continue with detailed enumerations of the various dhammas according to these categories.

Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object and is not a root-cause, there arises a state that does not have the Path as its object and is not a root-cause, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition: thirty-five; under object-condition: twenty-six ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition: thirty-five.

Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object and is not a root-cause, there arises a state that does not have the Path as its root-cause and is not a root-cause, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition: twenty-six ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition: twenty-six.
